statement: For every integer b>=2, finitely supported rational probability distribution p on positive integer horizons, and rational R>=rho_b=b^b/(b^b-(b-1)^b), the explicit algorithm in evidence/prefix_oracle.py, with max_chord_probes=0, returns a law f minimizing sum_x p_x E_f C_T(x), subject to E_f C_T(x)<=R min(x,b) for every integer x>=1, with C_t(x)=x for t>x and b+t-1 otherwise. Its support is contained in {1,...,b} union {d+1:p_d>0,d>=b}, with at most two support days >=b. It also returns rational lambda>=0, y_x>=0 (1<=x<b), and alpha satisfying g(t)+lambda(t-1)+sum_{x=t}^{b-1}(b+t-1-x)y_x>=alpha for all positive integer t, and J_p(f)=alpha-(R-1)sum_{x=1}^{b-1}x y_x-lambda(R-1)b, certifying global optimality. After computing g on this finite set S, the algorithm makes O(log Z) calls to an O(b^2+|S|)-arithmetic-operation oracle, where D=b! b^b, H=q_p q_R D, L=b+max S, Z=2 L H^4, q_R is the denominator of R and q_p is the least common multiple of the probability denominators. Intermediate bit lengths and total bit time are polynomial in numerical b and the binary input length; no polynomial-in-log(b), strongly polynomial, or complete arbitrary-forecast Pareto-frontier enumeration claim is made. The accompanying exact separation at b=3,R=3/2,p_1=2/5,p_2=3/5 has global expected optimum 39/20, minimum feasible raw support-cost level 14/5, and best expected cost within that minimum level 11/5, isolating the Appendix D.2 support-threshold optimality inference in arXiv:2603.29233v1. In addition, for the uniform forecast on {1,...,b}, put a=b-1, r=R-1, m=(b+1)/2, z_i=b^(i-1)/a^i, C_0=A_0=0, A_j=(b/a)^j-1, C_j=(2b-j)(b/a)^j-2b, and r_j=b/(b+C_j) for j=0,...,b. Then r_0=1>...>r_b=rho_b-1. For r_j<=r<=r_{j-1}, the unique optimal law is f_i=r*z_i for i<j, f_j=[b-r*(b+C_{j-1})]/(b+1-j), f_{b+1}=1-sum_{i<=j}f_i, all other masses zero. At shared endpoints the formulas agree; for r>=1 the deterministic buy-day b+1 is optimal. Writing d_i=(b+1-i)*(b+i-2)/(2b), lambda_j=(b+j-2)/(2b), s_j=sum_{i<j}d_i*z_i-lambda_j*(b+C_{j-1}), the value on segment j is m+lambda_j*b+s_j*r. It has exactly b strictly decreasing affine pieces and the plateau R>=2. The compact shared frontier representation and one policy/value/dual query each use O(b) rational arithmetic operations; every rational has O(b*log(b)+len(R)) bits. For every b and r_b<r<r_{b-1}, this unique optimum has all b+1 masses on {1,...,b+1} strictly positive, so b+1 total support and two support days >=b are necessary simultaneously. This policy is the already-known KF26 C.1(ii) one-hot-b capped-geometric optimizer when r<=1-1/b, and another one-hot-b optimum thereafter; no new canonical policy family or first support-pattern priority is claimed. The supplementary exact objective separation at b=3,R=3/2,p_1=p_2=1/2 has unique expected-cost optimizer (f_1,f_3)=(1/4,3/4), J=15/8, and unique expected-per-horizon-ratio optimizer (f_2,f_3)=(1/2,1/2), ratio=5/4; their other-objective values are 21/16 and 2. The KF26 criticism targets the arXiv v1 D.2 support-level inference; the forced 11/5 prescription cost is not asserted to be a uniquely specified literal Algorithm 3 implementation output. This combined submission additionally extends the same counterexample to the precisely identified published version, Kim--Fan, ICML 2026, PMLR 306:57411--57444, whose complete 560062-byte PDF has SHA-256 5c5842ff3d0d2df8b802bc9968d520410ade6a059f83b3ca9fb1ac6a8f53ec4c. Its Sections 5.1--5.2 use the same cost, expected objective and all-integer-horizon robustness; printed-page-30 Appendix D.2 retains the expected-cost/minimum-feasible-raw-support-level inference refuted above. The official publisher page links the software repository distributional-ski-rental. At pinned commit 0a86125f31e9e1b1abbba5bd4fde32a332860124, both named Python source files, bound by their full hashes in revision/published-extension-provenance.json, were executed only through unchanged SkiRentalOptimizer class AST nodes. For literal constructor arguments (3,1.5,[1,2],[.4,.6]) and each tolerance 1e-5,1e-9,1e-12, solve followed by construct_policy_pmf returned the binary-exact law (f_1,f_2,f_3)=(1/4,3/8,3/8), with returned levels respectively 3.000001907348633,3.0000000004656613,2.9999999999995453 in both files. These are six finite floating-point software observations, independently repeated by a separate loader within this research pass, not a universal claim about versions, tolerances or convergence. Exact evaluation of this returned law under rational forecast (2/5,3/5) and the original cost gives J=12/5, E(T-1)=9/8, raw support maximum 3 and genuine R=3/2 robustness for every integer actual horizon. Both classes returned False at is_feasible(14/5) and True at is_feasible(3) in the documented calls, despite the exactly certified feasible support-level law at 14/5. Literal line traces at h=3 distinguish the two methods: construct_policy_pmf temporarily assigns day-3 mass 9/16 and reaches internal F=19/16, then its existing normalization correction reduces the day-3 mass to 3/8. No repair of third-party code is used. Thus 39/20 is the mathematical global optimum, 11/5 is the mathematical cost at the minimum feasible raw-support level 14/5, and 12/5 is the observed pinned-software cost. The refined literal trace supersedes the informal handoff shorthand for intermediate construction states; the original accepted proofs, optimizer code and their bounds are unchanged.
contribution: One coherent revised result note: the prior general certifying optimizer repairs the raw support-level inference, with a rigorous pure-bisection scope, complete elimination and intermediate-bit proofs, plus a closed-form uniform objective frontier and strict-dual uniqueness/support-necessity analysis. Generic finite LP already gives polynomial bit time, so no asymptotic advantage is asserted. The underlying uniform optimal policy overlaps exactly with the known one-hot-b construction; that structure and geometric recurrences are credited, and the uniform extension alone is not assumed sufficient for publication. The precise KF26 trace separates its stated prescription from ambiguous literal code. New independent finite attacks and current primary comparisons support fresh scrutiny, not priority or mathematical acceptance. The full original arbitrary-forecast frontier task remains unresolved. A new frozen scope and fresh referee must assess correctness and substantive value before any new manuscript or release. The only new scope in research pass 3 is the published-source application of the already-proved separation and a reproducible, commit/hash-bound finite software observation. It prevents misreporting 11/5 as actual author-code output, certifies the true returned-law cost 12/5 and robustness directly, and records the unmodified construction normalization trace. It adds no new algorithmic, uniform-frontier, complexity or priority theorem. The previous referee explicitly excluded these facts, so acceptance of the preceding snapshot does not certify the new combined claim.
